chat.author: Ted Lemon
chat.text: "Daleks here in Dinozop"

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: draft-lemon-exterminate-exterminate-exterminate

chat.author: Benno Overeinder
chat.text: Apologies for the rush during the opening.  But we could easily fill 1:30 hour in the one hour given.  :-)

chat.author: Andrew Campling
chat.text: Surely that's always true for any DNSOPs meeting, irrespective of the time slot?  :-)

chat.author: Benno Overeinder
chat.text: True!

chat.author: Andrew Campling
chat.text: So at least rough consensus and running code?

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: One can ask for specific RFC numbers, so these could be paired even if the parent-centric draft gets published 4 years from now....

chat.author: Benjamin Schwartz
chat.text: @Shane I think parent-centric behavior is actually easier to resolve, since you always know exactly what NS RRset it's using, and you can query it directly from the parent if you care.

chat.author: Benjamin Schwartz
chat.text: s/resolve/debug/

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: I think the thing is that the resolver may have cached the parent NS RRset earlier (like 20 hours ago) and you can't know what it thinks the parent NS RRset it.

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: I agree with Ben. It massively reduces removes the 'quantum state' of cache/uncertainity when debugging.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: But maybe some sort of EDNS option along the style of NSID, but instead asking for resolution information makes more sense than "cache snooping".

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: (That would obviously be outside of the scope of the parent-centric draft).

chat.author: Ralf Weber
chat.text: Shane the child NS record also has a TTL and might be change - that is a generic "problem" of DNS

chat.author: Andrew Campling
chat.text: On Catalog Zones: for background on the topic, see a discussion with the authors and others at https://419.consulting/encrypted-dns/f/dns-catalog-zones-a-sharp-knife-in-the-toolkit

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: I think the problem can be solved relatively easily by adding a way to query for parent-side NS. We will just spent a year or two arguing about the color of bikeshed.

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: As an example - when asked with RD=0 it could give back cached child-side NS in ANSWER section, and cached parent-side NS in AUTHORITY section. It is RD=0, nobody cares what it does (on resolver) anyway.

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: If we want to punch a simple hole then cache-snooping can always return delegation-NS instead of state of the cache.

chat.author: Ralf Weber
chat.text: I'm not sure if I want to make this delegation information available to anyone querying, but it should certainly be available to the operator of the server.

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: It could be "MAY"

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: Can be MAY. Can require TSIG key or any other sort of ACL. After all RD=0 queries are not generally available from resolver even today - see Unbound's ACL.

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: But I like the idea of RD=0 returning both. That's simple and implementable.

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: Well again. We can paint it in all colors of rainbow, and I don't think it matters what color it has in the end.

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: I can see "local policy" in blinking letters in front of my eyes when I think about it.

chat.author: Ralf Weber
chat.text: RD=0 has a know behaviour, maybe make it a CHAOS class query ( :see_no_evil: :wink: ), but yeah it has to be limited in access

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: Return it only for RD=0 QTYPE=ANY :troll:

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: If we really really wanted we could just get new (meta) QTYPE=parent-side-NS. Again - rainbow.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: Including the serial in catalog zones would be awesome.

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text:
RD=0 has a know behaviour

But will anything actually break by adding extra NS RRset to AUTHORITY section?

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: It will not break anything which is not broken today. Non-minimal responses already do supply NSes in AUTHORITY section even if ANSWER is non-empty.

chat.author: Ralf Weber
chat.text: Don't think so, but of course have not tested it, especially as RD=0 is rare

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: I prefer explicit signalling. Adding an EDNS option seems useful here.

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: If we thought AUTHORITY is too dangerous (I don't see why it would be, but still) it can go to ADDITIONAL, too.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: Or the QTYPE that Petr suggested.

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: The explicit signaling feels like a separate draft though.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: Yes, it can be.

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: Also we can just leave it undefined as it is server-debugging feature and so far we did not standardize this at all.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: A lot of people have something to say about this draft. :sweat_smile:

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: Isn't this all solved by pre-fetch before expiration?

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: I just checked and BIND has prefetch since 2014.

chat.author: Valentin Goșu
chat.text: I don't think applications have a way to do prefetch, can they?

chat.author: Sebastian Poreba
chat.text: Pre-fetch doesn't work for applications that are not running. Mobile use case optimises first request latency

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: Pre-fetch on the _resolver_ side.

chat.author: Ralf Weber
chat.text: There are reasons why you might not have prefetched the data

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: I mean re-looking up a reord before the TTL expires.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: Bold assertion: IGNORE TTL

chat.author: Valentin Goșu
chat.text: if the application resolves it before it expires, it would still get the same about to expire record, right?

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: That's why it needs to be pre-feteched on the resolver side. As BIND has apparently been able to do since 2014.

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: I mean this: https://bind9.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference.html#namedconf-statement-prefetch

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: The prefetch only works if someone asks for the name though.

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: Current implementation of it, yes. There's many ways to paint this bikeshed too :-)

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: For popular names, I think an approach that is worth a draft for recommending the combination of recursive doing prefetch and clients being willing to go enough past the TTL to avoid race conditions with short TTLs.

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: The prefetch in the resolver, I mean. The resolver does not prefetch anything pro-actively, only when there's a query for a name and the answer is close to expiry.

chat.author: Ralf Weber
chat.text:
What Ondrey said 
 and if the packet reaches the server that was asked before

chat.author: Dan York
chat.text: Okay... so this reference of RSS is NOT the "Rich Site Summary" that we use for creating feeds of blogs and websites and such. :scream:

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: Anyway, this draft doesn't have to be on Standards track, it could land in Informational to describe what the end devices are doing.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: Prefetch _could_ work without someone asking for the name. Of course if nobody is asking for it then I'm not sure it is actually operationally very important....

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: (Again, in the resolver.)

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: Can be even based on query frequency of :crystal_ball: , too.

chat.author: Benjamin Schwartz
chat.text: "Prefetch anything that had a cache hit in the last TTL" seems like a plausible policy.

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: For the longer-time-scale (eg, ignoring TTLs by multiple orders of magnitude and expanding to hours/days) there are fewer clients doing this today and I think it would be operationally bad to encourage more of this without an explicit opt-in (via a SvcParam or similar to say what is safe happy-eyeballs-wise).  The sad reality is that just because a server does a TLS successful handshake doesn't mean it is intended to be an active instance.  (eg, it might be no longer getting config updates, it might be under maintenance and about to restart, etc).

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: I sense next F5 product line is going to have DNS Optimizer with Crystal-Ball-On-Chip :tm: .

chat.author: Oskar Mansfeld
chat.text: For what its worth Firefox moved from 1min to 10min grace period last year and we already saw good improvements in p75 and p95 dns lookup time from that comparatively small value.

chat.author: Mike Blanche
chat.text: +1 Erik - just because a server is responding doesn't mean it's a good destination

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: Well another option is to just make 7706 and 8806 Historic and be done with prescribing implementations what to do as this is a pure optimization.

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text:
Prefetch anything that had a cache hit in the last TTL

For a large resolver yes, for my home resolver, it will just keep the resolver busy.
Also there are memory impllications as you need to store the "this was queried and needs to be prefetched". These lists can be kept thread-local, so we can avoid the contention, but still - actively keeping the list of stuff to be prefetched has a singnificant implementation impact.

chat.author: Valentin Goșu
chat.text:
Mike Blanche said:

+1 Erik - just because a server is responding doesn't mean it's a good destination

Just because the DNS records changed, doesn't mean the client will check the DNS records and close the connection. At the moment I don't think there's a good way to signal that "you shouldn't really use the old IPs anymore"

chat.author: Dragana Damjanovic
chat.text: the TTL is this signal.

chat.author: Warren Kumari
chat.text: Just to follow on from what Wes said, draft-wkumari-dnsop-localroot-bcp - "Populating resolvers with the root zone" jsut says "We don't care  what yo do, you should just look like somehow you have the the info"

chat.author: Mark Andrews
chat.text: What's needed a discussion of how to support DNS in the enterprise properly including trust anchors.

chat.author: Warren Kumari
chat.text: Implmentors know how to do stuff, we explicitly want them to decide what works best in their implmentation
